engine.description: Rules are declarative IF-THEN productions. Conditions are ANDed. Rules fire once. Derived facts feed later rules, which is what produces a visible forward-chaining trace.

rules.title: Sadness is present

conditions.label: You described sadness or low mood

rules.why: Sadness on its own is enough to plan gentle, mood-supportive options. It is not treated as a diagnosis.

rules.title: Sadness has persisted for weeks or longer

conditions.label: It has lasted weeks or longer

rules.why: Duration changes the support plan: persistent low mood calls for a steadier routine and a lower threshold for professional advice.

rules.title: Anxiety is causing arousal

conditions.label: It is moderately or strongly distressing

rules.why: Moderate-to-high anxiety responds first to settling the body, before problem-solving.

rules.title: Panic-like activation

conditions.label: You described panic or sudden intense fear

then.value: Panic can feel alarming in the body. If this is new chest pain or breathing difficulty, seek medical care; otherwise a slow, gentle grounding exercise is a reasonable first step.

rules.why: Panic is given near-top priority because the body feels unsafe even when there is no immediate danger.

rules.title: Stress is creating load
rules.why: Stress is framed as load to manage, not as a personal failing.

rules.title: Overwhelm is present
rules.why: Overwhelm needs a smaller scope before any productivity suggestion.

rules.title: Loneliness is present
rules.why: Loneliness is treated as a connection need, not something to 'get over'.

rules.title: Loneliness with little support

conditions.label: You have little or no one to talk to

rules.why: Limited support changes the plan: the app should not assume a friend is available and should include helplines as a real option.

rules.title: Reported sleep difficulty
rules.why: Sleep is treated as a foundation habit that affects mood and energy.

rules.title: Sleep duration is low

conditions.label: You are sleeping less than 6 hours

rules.why: Short sleep is a concrete, modifiable factor worth addressing gently.

rules.title: Motivation deficit
rules.why: Low motivation is treated as depletion, not laziness.

rules.title: Rumination or harsh self-talk

conditions.label: You described harsh self-talk or negative thinking

rules.why: Thinking patterns are addressed with gentle distance and self-compassion, not argument or forced positivity.

rules.title: Anger activation
rules.why: Anger gets a pause-and-release plan rather than suppression or judgement.

rules.title: Grief process
rules.why: Grief is not pathologised; the plan makes room for it and checks support.

rules.title: Study or work overload

conditions.label: You described study or work pressure

rules.why: Academic pressure is handled with structure and bounded effort, not more pressure.

rules.title: Burnout risk
rules.why: Exhaustion that rest has not fixed calls for recovery and load reduction, not optimisation.

rules.title: Relationship strain
rules.why: Relationship pain is acknowledged before any communication advice.

rules.title: Social anxiety pattern

conditions.label: You described fear of social judgement

rules.why: Social anxiety is met with small, voluntary steps and no forced exposure.

rules.title: High self-reported distress
rules.why: High distress changes priority: comfort and safety come before activities.

rules.title: Several concerns at once

conditions.label: You named three or more separate concerns

rules.why: When several concerns overlap, a single small starting point is more useful than a long plan.

rules.title: Low mood calls for behavioural activation
rules.why: Small, value-guided action is a well-established self-help approach for low mood; the rule deliberately keeps actions tiny.

rules.title: Persistent low mood needs a steadier plan
rules.why: When low mood persists, consistent routines help, and it is reasonable to have a professional conversation as well.

rules.title: Anxious arousal needs grounding
rules.why: Grounding is offered before cognitive work while the body is activated.

rules.title: Panic needs immediate grounding
rules.why: Panic is met first with a brief, concrete settling exercise.

rules.title: Stress load needs rest and structure
rules.why: Stress often improves when both demand and recovery are addressed, not when the person simply tries harder.

rules.title: Overwhelm needs a smaller scope
rules.why: Reducing the next step to one concrete action is the safest response to feeling flooded.

rules.title: Loneliness needs connection
rules.why: The plan should create one low-pressure point of contact, not demand a social overhaul.

rules.title: High isolation needs support options
rules.why: When a trusted person is not available, helplines and counsellors are legitimate sources of connection.

rules.title: Sleep debt needs sleep support
rules.why: A small, repeatable wind-down is more realistic than a perfect sleep schedule.

rules.title: Motivation deficit needs a tiny start
rules.why: Action tends to come before motivation, so the suggested action is deliberately small.

rules.title: Rumination needs a different relationship with thoughts

conditions.label: Harsh self-talk or rumination is established

rules.why: The aim is distance and fairness, not arguing someone out of their feelings.

rules.title: Anger needs safe release
rules.why: A pause protects the person and the people around them; release can come through words or movement.

rules.title: Grief needs room and support
rules.why: Grief support should not rush the person toward 'moving on'.

rules.title: Study overload needs structure

conditions.label: Study or work overload is established

rules.why: One bounded focus block lowers the entry cost compared with a large plan.

rules.title: Burnout needs recovery
rules.why: Recovery and load reduction come before any suggestion to be more productive.

rules.title: Relationship strain needs reflection and support
rules.why: Naming what happened and staying connected to safe people are gentler than advice to confront anyone.

rules.title: Social anxiety needs grounding and small steps
rules.why: The plan combines settling the body with optional, very small social steps.

rules.title: High distress prioritises comfort
rules.why: When distress is high, coping and rest come before reflection or tasks.

rules.title: Multiple concerns call for one starting point
rules.why: A professional can help hold the whole picture; the app should not try to solve everything at once.

rules.title: Grounding options
rules.why: Breathing and sensory grounding are brief, low-risk, and usable immediately.

rules.title: Behavioural activation options
rules.why: The options create a small completed action without requiring motivation first.

rules.title: Connection options
rules.why: One low-pressure message is easier to act on than 'be more social'.

rules.title: Sleep support options
rules.why: A wind-down routine and a small screen boundary are practical sleep supports.

rules.title: Reflection options for rumination
rules.why: Writing and a fairer inner sentence create distance without denying the feeling.

rules.title: Rest and recovery options
rules.why: Recovery is treated as part of the plan, not a reward for finishing everything.

rules.title: Structure options
rules.why: A single next step and a bounded block reduce overwhelm without adding pressure.

rules.title: Emotional release options
rules.why: The options give strong feeling somewhere to go without harming anyone.

rules.title: Professional support is an option
rules.why: A referral is offered as an additional option, never as proof that self-help failed.

rules.title: Basic care when depleted
rules.why: Very small physical care steps are added only as low-ranked extras, so they never crowd out the main suggestion.

rules.title: Low energy favours gentle options
rules.why: When energy is low, the app adds only low-effort options; it does not tell the person to try harder.

rules.title: Little time available
rules.why: Suggestions are sized to the time the user actually has.

rules.title: Preference for outdoors or movement
rules.why: Recommendations are matched to activities the person already values.

rules.title: Preference for social contact
rules.why: A preferred channel makes follow-through easier.

rules.title: Preference for quiet activities
rules.why: Quiet options are added when they fit the person's stated preference.

rules.title: Preference for creative expression
rules.why: Creative options are offered when the person already uses them.

rules.title: Limited support changes connection options
rules.why: The plan does not assume a friend is available, and includes formal support as a real option.

rules.title: Anxiety plus sleep debt
rules.why: When anxiety and poor sleep overlap, calming before bed matters more than a long activity list.

rules.title: Long duration plus severe impact

conditions.label: It has lasted a month or more
It is strongly affecting daily life

then.value: What you are describing has lasted a while and is affecting daily life. A counsellor or doctor can help you understand what is going on and what options exist. This app cannot diagnose.

rules.why: Persistent difficulties with major daily impact deserve assessment by a qualified person.

rules.title: Persistent low mood with sleep debt
rules.why: Low mood and sleep problems that persist together are worth discussing with a professional. This is a support prompt, not a diagnosis.

rules.title: Prolonged grief

conditions.label: It has lasted a month or more

then.value: Grief has no deadline, but if it is lasting a long time and making daily life very hard, grief-informed counselling can help.

rules.why: Prolonged grief can benefit from specialised support; the wording avoids pathologising normal grief.

rules.title: After a safety check, keep support open

conditions.label: You confirmed you are safe right now

then.value: Being safe right now matters, and so does what happens next. Please keep the helpline numbers somewhere visible and consider telling one trusted person about today.

rules.why: A safety check is not a closed case. The plan stays supportive and includes professional options.

rules.title: Shared high distress

conditions.label: More than one concern is present

rules.why: Multiple concerns at high distress are beyond what a self-help tool should try to hold alone.
